overall: Los Angeles is finishing a warm but moderate July day, with temperatures having plateaued at 71.6°F since approximately 14:00 ET — roughly 1.8 hours ago. Conditions are mostly sunny with only 12% cloud fraction and light southwest winds around 10 mph, consistent with a typical marine-influenced summer pattern. The day has trended slightly warmer than some model guidance (notably NBM at 69.1°F) but has essentially stopped climbing, suggesting the daily peak is likely in or very near.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models show meaningful spread: HRRR is the outlier high at 72.7°F, GFS sits at 71.9°F, ECMWF at 70.6°F, and NBM at 69.1°F — the observed running max of 71.6°F has already eclipsed NBM and ECMWF, lending credibility to GFS as the best-calibrated model today. The INTRADAY model is placing 100% probability on the 72–73°F even bucket and the META model agrees at 90.4%, suggesting the ensemble expects at least a fractional additional rise above 71.6°F, though the flat velocity (+0.0°F/hr) and post-peak timing temper that expectation.
max_temp_prediction: With the running max already at 71.6°F, flat temperature velocity, and the estimated peak hour already passed (~14:00 ET), the final TMAX is most likely to land in the 71–72°F range of the active odd bucket set. A push to just touch 72°F is plausible given GFS (71.9°F) and the INTRADAY model signals, but crossing firmly into the 73–74°F odd bucket would require unexpected re-warming that current observations do not support. Confidence is moderately high: the 71–72°F odd bucket holds the plurality probability at 37.2% and aligns well with observed conditions; the best point estimate is approximately 71.8°F.
